key_insight: Under cross-dataset shift, chest X-ray models lost predictive performance, and source-fitted temperature scaling increased confidence in incorrect predictions.
clinical_relevance: Strong benchmark performance and calibrated source-domain confidence may not indicate reliable predictions at another hospital.
method: Trained ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121 on CheXpert and evaluated transfer to MIMIC-CXR.
Assessed pneumothorax and pleural effusion using AUC, ECE, Brier score, and confidence on incorrect predictions.
Tested source-validation temperature scaling and examined attention patterns with Grad-CAM.
evidence_signal: Across five experimental settings, cross-domain AUC dropped 7–13 percentage points; metrics were reported with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.
watch_item: Evidence covers two architectures, two pathologies, and one transfer direction; broader reliability requires validation across additional sites and tasks.
paper_title: When Should We Trust Medical Image Models? Evaluating Confidence Reliability under Cross-Dataset Shift
